title: Coefficient dual as a limit of its strict quotient Hom tower
statement: For any prime l and finite extension E/Q_l, put R=integralDualizingCoefficients l E. On the whole unbounded ordinary module derived category D(R), there is a natural isomorphism integralDualizingCoefficientHomTower l E ⋙ CoefTower.totalLimit R ≅ coefficientDerivedDual R. This assertion has no scheme, compact-support functor or geometric dualizing tower among its hypotheses.

proof.text: The actual positive coefficient quotient tower has surjective transitions and ordinary limit R, with its quotient projections, by completeness. Recursively lifting x_n-b_n proves 1-shift surjective; hence the quotient tower in degree zero has derived limit R[0].

For a K-flat representative P of any C and one simultaneous K-injective resolution I of the quotient tower, the closed Hom from constant P is Hom(P,I_n). Its resolved transitions split and Hom(P,lim I)=lim Hom(P,I_n), with all differentials. Localization and precomposition compatibility give a natural isomorphism with RHom_R(C,R[0]), the coefficient derived dual. The localization equivalence changes only the model of the same complexes.

theorem integralDualizing_coefficient_hom_tower_limit :

        coefficientDerivedDual (integralDualizingCoefficients l E))
